prompt:
Image 1 is the camera and pose guide: grey clay maquettes in exactly this grid, rendered from the game's battle camera; the coloured areas on them mark where the side's cloth goes. Copy from it exactly the camera angle, the direction every figure faces, the pose in each cell, the size and the position of the figure in its cell and the grid. Do not copy its smooth grey clay surfaces, its simple shapes or its toy-like proportions.
Image 2 is a finished sprite sheet of the whole Wolf Rider, rider and wolf together, painted at the right camera: match its camera, its daylight, its painting and the size of the wolf in each cell; paint no rider: the saddle is empty.
Image 3 is a painted portrait from the same game, a reference for the painting style only: do not paint that person or copy its background, candlelight or framing.

A game sprite sheet: 16 full-length painted figures of one saddled war wolf, one figure in each cell of a 4 by 4 grid, on a perfectly flat, uniform pure blue (#0000FF) background. The same saddled war wolf, the same equipment, the same colours and the same scale in every cell; only the pose changes.

The last attempt painted every wolf in profile, from the side and at eye level, and much too large. Paint each wolf as seen from high above and in front, exactly as in Images 1 and 2: we look down on the top of its head and its back, see its face from above and its chest, its legs short and foreshortened; it is as small in its cell as in Image 2. 

Camera: high above and in front, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at miniatures on a table; orthographic, with no perspective, so every figure is the same size. Every figure faces toward us and toward the lower left of the image. The figures are foreshortened as seen from above.

Light: outdoor daylight. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the tops of helmets and hoods, the shoulders and the upper-left side of every figure with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows, nothing glows unless the description below says so. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, the same hand as the painted portrait references; a muted earthy palette of charcoal, ash grey, dull iron, bark brown, leather and bone, in which the side's cloth is the one clear hue; soft painterly edges, with small crisp highlights on metal edges and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges of every figure. Each figure has a strong, simple, readable silhouette that still reads when the figure is shrunk to 40 pixels tall. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The figure: a War Wolf of the Thornwood, saddled but with no rider: a real, huge timber wolf, its shoulder as high as a man's chest, long legs, a deep narrow chest, a long muzzle, pointed ears, a bushy tail; a thick dark grey-brown coat, darker along the spine, warm grey and brown, never pink or violet. On its back a large pine-green saddle cloth with a broad pale bone-coloured border, from the shoulders to the hips and hanging low on both flanks, under a small empty bark saddle; a pine-green quilted cloth bib over its chest under a narrow bark-plate harness. The green is a clean, clearly coloured pine green that catches the sun, like fresh fir needles, never blackish, olive, grey or teal-blue.

Nobody rides it: the saddle is empty in every cell, and there is no person anywhere on the sheet. Facing, again: every wolf faces toward us and to the lower left, the hit and falling ones included.

The cells, left to right, row by row (the poses of the camera and pose guide):
1. (row 1, column 1) the wolf standing square on all four paws, head up and ears forward.
2. (row 1, column 2) the wolf loping, front paws reaching.
3. (row 1, column 3) the wolf loping, legs gathered.
4. (row 1, column 4) the wolf leaping, front paws off the ground.
5. (row 2, column 1) the wolf landing from a leap, front paws down, hind legs high.
6. (row 2, column 2) the wolf at full gallop, stretched out, charging toward the lower left.
7. (row 2, column 3) the wolf crouched low on its haunches, about to spring.
8. (row 2, column 4) the wolf lunging forward, head low.
9. (row 3, column 1) the wolf biting: head lunged forward, jaws wide open.
10. (row 3, column 2) the wolf flinching sideways from a hit.
11. (row 3, column 3) the wolf stumbling, its front legs buckling.
12. (row 3, column 4) the wolf lying dead on its side.
13. (row 4, column 1) the wolf lying dead, a different sprawl.
14. (row 4, column 2) the wolf bolting at a gallop, extended.
15. (row 4, column 3) the wolf bolting at a gallop, gathered.
16. (row 4, column 4) the wolf with its head thrown up, howling.

Background and separation: one flat pure blue (#0000FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow; at least 24 pixels of clean background between any two figures and around the edges. No blue, violet or purple anywhere on the figures.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; extra people; cropped or overlapping figures.
